title: AI: A* Grid Pathfinding
summary: Implement A* search on a grid with obstacles - the classic planning problem behind game AI and robot navigation.
problemStatement:
## Scenario
A warehouse robot moves on a rectangular grid. Cells are either free (`0`) or blocked (`1`). Implement **A\*** so it can plan the shortest route.

## Task
In `pathfinding.py` implement `astar(grid, start, goal)`:

- `grid` is a non-empty list of equal-length rows of `0`/`1`. `start` and `goal` are `(row, col)` tuples.
- Movement is 4-directional (up, down, left, right), each step costs 1, no diagonals.
- Return the path as a list of `(row, col)` tuples **including** `start` and `goal`. It must be a **shortest** path.
- Return `None` when the goal cannot be reached.
- If `start == goal` (and the cell is free) return `[start]`.
- Raise `ValueError` if the grid is empty or ragged, or `start` / `goal` is outside the grid or on a blocked cell.

Use the Manhattan distance as your heuristic. Any correct shortest path is accepted when several exist.

requirements.title: Return a valid path
requirements.description: Starts at start, ends at goal, only 4-neighbour steps through free cells.

requirements.title: Path is shortest
requirements.description: The returned path has the minimum possible length.

requirements.title: Detect unreachable goals
requirements.description: Returns None when no route exists.

requirements.title: Validate input
requirements.description: ValueError for bad grids or endpoints.
